articles.title: OpenAI to announce "o" always-on agent during DevDay
articles.desc: What do we know so far? OpenAI is preparing a new consumer-facing agent called "o" for release, according to the latest leaks.
articles.content: OpenAI to announce "o" always-on agent during DevDay OpenAI appears to be preparing an always-on agent that could launch as “O,” with DevDay on September 29 emerging as a possible announcement window. OpenAI has confirmed that DevDay takes place that day in San Francisco, with Sam Altman opening the keynote. We have spotted references to "O" across ChatGPT’s configuration, including “O” as a display name and an email suffix configured as “-o.” The agent was also recently referenced as a benefit on the upgrade page for the $100 Pro plan. Together, these clues point to a persistent agent designed to keep working outside a normal chat session, potentially with its own email identity from the start. The project may be related to “Aeon,” a name previously associated with OpenAI’s always-on agent work. Aeon is also being used internally around accounts, suggesting that "O" could become a consumer-facing implementation built on related infrastructure. Details about supported tasks, permissions, scheduling, memory, or availability remain unknown. Two other clues point to the "O" branding. OpenAI has previously been rumored to be exploring a , making the single-letter name an interesting potential reference if those projects eventually intersect. Meanwhile, the @o account on X currently appears suspended and could potentially be reserved for a future launch. An always-on agent would fit OpenAI’s broader move from conversational toward software that can carry out longer-running work with less supervision. It would primarily benefit users who want agents handling recurring research, communications, monitoring, or other tasks while they are away. Meta has already pushed this category forward with Muse, putting additional pressure on to show what its own persistent agent can do. It will be part
articles.content: India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 has introduced a new initiative called Viksit Tech 47. The program will identify and honor Indian technology companies, leaders, and innovators who are shaping the country's tech industry. Viksit Tech 47 supports the larger Viksit Bharat 2047 vision . It will be part of the 10th edition of IMC, set to run from October 7 to 10 at Yashobhoomi Convention Centre in New Delhi. What Areas Viksit Tech 47 Will Cover The initiative spans several segments. These include consumer devices, wearables, audio, video and surveillance, connected mobility, smart home and IoT, components and manufacturing, artificial intelligence and deep tech, and software as a service (SaaS) platforms. As part of the program, IMC 2026 will release a flagship report studying more than 200 Indian technology companies. Techarc is the research partner for this study. The report will look at India's place in the global technology value chain, with input from founders and industry experts. The platform also includes the Dr. Zarabi Indigenization Award for Startups. This award will honor firms working on product design, engineering, components, and manufacturing. The focus is on startups building hardware, gadgets, devices, and appliances in areas where India has historically depended on imports. Also Read: Mercedes-Maybach S-Class India Launch Set for October 5 Awards and Scale of the Event Viksit Tech 47 will also recognize brands, leaders, and ecosystem enablers through several award categories. These include Viksit Tech Brand of the Year, Viksit Tech Leader of the Year, and Viksit Tech Enabler of the Year. IMC 2026 is expected to draw more than 1.5 lakh attendees. Over 300 exhibitors and partners from more than 100 countries are set to take part. The event will also showcase more than 1,500 technology use cases. The initiative now covers hardware, AI, manufacturing, IoT, and software as well. It aims to give Indian technology businesses a stronger platform for recognition, both at home and abroad.

articles.title: Spacetech startup GalaxEye secures Rs 64 crore govt support to develop OptoSAR satellite
articles.desc: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye Space Solutions is set to receive Rs 63.84 crore in financial support from the Indian government to develop a multisensor satellite capable of producing OptoSAR imagery at a resolution finer than 0.5 metres. The Technology Development Board (TDB), under the
articles.content: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye Space Solutions is set to receive Rs 63.84 crore in financial support from the Indian government to develop a multisensor satellite capable of producing OptoSAR imagery at a resolution finer than 0.5 metres. The Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), has signed an agreement with GalaxEye for the support under the government's Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project has a total approved cost of Rs 247.69 crore and aims to take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to TRL 9. The financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debentures. The government said the funding will help GalaxEye undertake further development, engineering, testing and validation as it moves the technology towards deployment. How GalaxEye's OptoSAR technology works At the centre of the project is OptoSAR, GalaxEye's approach to combining Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Electro-Optical (EO) imaging. Optical imaging can provide detailed visual information about the Earth's surface, but its effectiveness can be affected by cloud cover and lighting conditions. SAR uses radar and can collect imagery through clouds and irrespective of daylight. GalaxEye's proposed system seeks to fuse information from both sensors to provide a more continuous picture of the Earth across different weather and lighting conditions. The proposed satellite is designed to provide imagery at a resolution finer than 0.5 metres. According to the government, potential applications include wide-area and long-range surveillance, human and vehicle detection, and target classification. “The support from the Technology Development Board under the RDI Fund will enable us to accelerate the development and validation of our OptoSAR technology. By combining SAR and optical sensing, we are working towards an Earth-observation capability that can provide high-resolution information across a wider range of weather and lighting conditions. This partnership will be important in taking the technology towards TRL-9 and its subsequent deployment,” promoters of GalaxEye said. From IIT Madras to Mission Drishti GalaxEye was founded in 2021 by Suyash Singh, Denil Chawda, Pranit Mehta, Kishan Thakkar and Rakshit Bhatt, who were part of a team of engineers at IIT Madras. The startup is developing Earth-observation systems that combine optical and radar sensing. Its first satellite, Mission Drishti, was launched on 3 May 2026 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9. At the time of the launch, the Indian government described Mission Drishti as the world's first OptoSAR satellite and India's largest privately built satellite. According to GalaxEye, the spacecraft was designed to combine optical and SAR sensors on a single platform. The mission later suffered a setback. In July, GalaxEye reported that communication with Drishti became intermittent during the final stage of its Launch and Early Orbit Phase before being lost. The company linked the anomaly to radiation effects associated with a geomagnetic solar storm that were likely to have affected a critical onboard system, while noting that an investigation into the precise cause was still under way. The satellite had completed a substantial part of its planned early-orbit activities and validated several spacecraft systems before communication was lost. It also said it planned to incorporate lessons from the mission into future spacecraft and target the launch of two more OptoSAR satellites within 24 months. In September, GalaxEye announced that it had secured a US patent for technology that synchronises optical and radar sensors, allowing them to collect spatially and temporally aligned Earth-observation data from the same satellite Government's Rs 1 lakh crore RDI programme The GalaxEye agreement comes under the government's wider RDI Scheme, which is aimed at increasing private-sector participation in research and development and supporting the commercialisation of indigenous technologies. The Union Cabinet approved the scheme on 1 July 2025 with an outlay of Rs 1 lakh crore over six years. It was formally launched on 3 November 2025. The programme provides long-term financing to eligible technology companies through debt and equity instruments and is intended to support research-driven and deep-tech projects. It operates through a two-tier structure. A Special Purpose Fund established within the Anusandhan National Research Foundation maintains the scheme's corpus and channels money through Second-Level Fund Managers. TDB and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council have been designated as Second-Level Fund Managers under the programme. As of July 2026, TDB had approved 22 projects with a combined project cost of Rs 4,744 crore and RDI Fund support of Rs 2,192 crore, according to the government. “India’s space ecosystem is entering a phase where the ability to develop and deploy sophisticated technologies within the country will be increasingly important. The RDI Fund provides an important mechanism to support such technology-intensive efforts through the critical stages between advanced development and deployment. The agreement with GalaxEye reflects TDB’s focus on enabling indigenous capabilities in emerging spacetech and supporting their journey towards commercialisation,” TDB Secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said.

articles.title: This Market Signal Has Been 95% Accurate for Nearly 90 Years. What Investors Need to Do Now to be Ready
articles.desc: The S&P 500 has seen positive returns in the 12 months after midterm elections 95% of the time since 1938.
articles.content: This Market Signal Has Been 95% Accurate for Nearly 90 Years. What Investors Need to Do Now to be Ready | United States Pick countries on the world map and get breaking news alerts in your browser — free, no app. The S&P 500 has seen positive returns in the 12 months after midterm elections 95% of the time since 1938. 10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index › One of the best predictors of stock market performance over the past nearly 90 years isn't some fancy valuation metric, like the Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio or Buffett indicator. Nor is it some complex macroeconomic forecast or interest rate model. It's actually the midterm elections. has had a positive performance one year after the midterm elections 95% of the time since 1938. The best thing is that it hasn't mattered which party wins, or whether the incumbents or challengers take more seats. The reason for this appears to be that the political uncertainty heading into the election fades after the votes are tallied. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. The market tends to dislike uncertainty and has generally taken a shoot-now-ask-questions-later mentality to major events. As such, it does make sense that once some of the uncertainty is lifted, stocks tend to outperform. In fact, not only have stocks gone up 95% of the time following midterm elections from November to November, but this is also historically the best year of returns in the election cycle. Since 1950, stocks have generated an average annual return of 14.5% during year three of a presidential cycle, which comes after the midterm elections. Ironically, the next-best period since 1950 is year four, with a 9.1% average annual return and a 72% chance the market goes up. However, year four is also the most unpredictable year, with the S&P 500 experiencing both large gains and losses. Year two of the cycle, meanwhile, tends to be the worst year for stocks, with an average return of 4.9% and only a 55% chance of a 12-month positive return since 1950. The September right ahead of the midterms tends to be a particularly tough stretch. According to Cantor Fitzgerald, the market has dropped in September by 5% or more in 15 of the past 24 midterm election years since 1930. However, Carson Group has noted that since 1950, October and November have been the best months for stocks during midterm election years, up 3% and 2.7%, respectively. UBS, meanwhile, has noted that during midterm election years, the market has rallied about 6% from the end of September through year-end. First, it would be foolish not to note that past patterns and historical performance are no guarantee of future outcomes. While a pattern clearly exists, from a statistical standpoint, the sample size would still be considered very small. That said, given this pattern and the current bull market, I think investors need to be invested. There has been a lot of talk this year about an AI bubble and a potential market crash, but this is not a time to sit on the sidelines. Yes, some valuation metrics like thesuggest that the S&P 500's market valuation is high, but the index's makeup is very different today than in the past. Gone are the days when the index was led by cyclical industrials, energy companies, and financials. Today, the S&P is dominated by large tech companies with less cyclical businesses, hugehas also changed the game, and the innovation curve is only getting steeper, meaning new technologies are being developed much more quickly than in the past. Unlike past tech innovation cycles, like PCs, the internet, and smartphones, AI growth is also not bound by human usage -- it's essentially limitless.index. articles.title: Pakistani MIT physicist calls for greater science and research investment in Karachi visit
articles.desc: Dr Nergis Mavalvala says curiosity and access to opportunity are key to scientific discovery
articles.content: MIT physicist calls for greater investment in science, research Pakistani MIT physicist calls for greater science and research investment in Karachi visit Dr Nergis Mavalvala says curiosity and access to opportunity are key to scientific discovery Pakistani-American physicist and MIT dean Dr Nergis Mavalvala speaks at the 10th Yohsin Lecture at Habib University in Karachi on Thursday. Photo: Express Pakistani-American physicist Dr Nergis Mavalvala has called for greater investment in scientific research, saying curiosity and access to opportunity were central to scientific discovery and that universities had a responsibility to nurture both. Speaking at Habib University on Thursday, Mavalvala, dean of the School of Science at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and a leading figure in the Nobel Prize-winning LIGO collaboration, said some of humanity’s most consequential discoveries had originated from questions with no immediate practical application. “Every single person at birth is research-minded,” she said during an extended question-and-answer session following her lecture. “The reason some of us get to do it in adulthood is [access to] opportunity.” Mavalvala was speaking at the 10th Yohsin Lecture, titled "The Joy of Discovery: Curiosity, Science, and the Pivotal Role of Universities", which drew an estimated 4,000 to 5,000 people to the university campus. Long queues formed as students, academics, alumni and members of the public gathered to hear the physicist speak about curiosity, scientific discovery and the role of universities in advancing knowledge. Reflecting on humanity’s longstanding fascination with the universe, Mavalvala said the impulse to explore was not necessarily driven by an immediate practical benefit. MIT dean Dr Nergis Mavalvala speaks during a panel discussion at Habib University in Karachi on Thursday. Photo: Express “Even pre-human cultures were looking up at the sky, in part because it was just mysterious,” she said. “A hundred years from now the only thing that will matter is that we’ve opened a new window into the universe.” She argued that universities should not be viewed merely as institutions for professional training, saying they also had a role in cultivating curiosity, creativity, perseverance and intellectual freedom. Mavalvala also stressed the importance of public and government investment in science and research. “Research has shown there is no investment that any government does that has greater return than investment in research and science,” she said. The lecture followed a two-day visit to Habib University during which Mavalvala met students, faculty, alumni and members of Pakistan’s scientific and business communities. She held discussions with faculty members on nurturing curiosity in classrooms and met science and humanities students from schools across Karachi. She also participated in sessions with the Entrepreneurs’ Organization and members of the scientific community. During her interaction with the university’s leadership, discussions also focused on the role of liberal arts education in developing students’ curiosity and the importance of teaching and mentorship. Habib University President Wasif Rizvi said the public response to the lecture demonstrated the value of making access to knowledge and leading thinkers more widely available. “This access had not been attempted in Pakistan before. It exists because the community in this room and outside decided that it should,” Rizvi said. He linked the initiative to the university’s philanthropic model, saying its students demonstrated what private philanthropy could achieve in expanding access to higher education. articles.title: How often you should wash your sheets and towels, according to science
articles.desc: Most people don't do it enough. The post How often you should wash your sheets and towels, according to science appeared first on Popular Science .
articles.content: How often you should wash your sheets and towels, according to science | Popular Science You’ve had a long day. You can’t wait to get home, take a hot shower, and climb into bed. Sounds wonderful, doesn’t it? Well, we hate to break it to you, but it could actually be incredibly gross. Naturally, everyone’s cleaning routines are different, so this isn’t a blanket statement (pardon the pun). Statistically speaking, most of us are not washing our bedding and bath things nearly enough. It’s generally recommended that people wash their bedsheets and bath towels every one to two weeks, but as a study conducted by showed the average person pushed it to around 24 days (25 for pillowcases alone). Single men tend to be worse, as , with a majority of them holding off on washing or changing bedsheets for four months. Think that’s gross? There are 5 percent of people overall who wash them once or twice…a year. “Every day we shed skin cells, and that is what dust mites feed on,” says allergy and immunology specialist . “So, regular removal of skin cells and dust mites with washing help to keep your bed—where you spend a third of your life—optimized.” Dr. Ho recommends that dust mite-sensitive patients follow the recommended cadence and wash sheets and bath towels every one to two weeks, using hot water specifically (or even a special “Sheets” or “Towels” setting, if your machine has those). While it’s easy to understand the need for this routine in terms of simple hygiene, what’s truly concerning is invisible to the naked eye. Germs, spores, and other kinds of particles live on every surface we come in contact with daily, even clean towels. Those shedding skin cells (which bacteria to munch on) and the wide range of organisms that can live on the human skin are rubbed off when we towel down, creating . You’re essentially creating a primordial soup of intermixing elements after every bath. To put it simply, you, your towels, and your sheets are all becoming distinct ecosystems full of germs and mites, which only grow the longer you go without laundering your items. And the impact can be wide-ranging, according to Dr. Ho, especially among the in the US who suffer from dust mite allergies. “Dust mite allergy contributes to asthma, allergic rhinitis, and even eczema flares,” she says. “These symptoms can not only affect quality of life but can have complications such as hospital visits for asthma, sinus infections, and super infections of the skin from flared eczema leading to scratching and excoriations of the skin.” So, yes, your cozy domicile can potentially be a Jurassic Park of microbes, mites, and germs the longer you put off your chores. For bedsheets, you’ll want to keep an eye out for visible stains, sweat marks, crumbs, dirt, or bugs, as well as a sticky or slimy feeling to the texture of the sheets, and, of course, odors. Smell is also one of the biggest red flags for bath towels. Your body may give you even clearer warning signs that it’s time to throw everything in the wash. “If your asthma or allergies are flared, and it has been more than a couple weeks since the last laundering, it’s best to prioritize laundering of these items right away,” advises Dr. Ho. And, please, do it at least once or twice a week. 2026 Popular Science Home of the Future Awards 39 products that will improve your everyday life.

articles.content: Rexel : Rexel annonce l'acquisition de GCG Rexel : Rexel annonce l'acquisition de GCG une plateforme de référence spécialisée dans les infrastructures aux Etats-Unis, une étape clé dans l’exécution de la stratégie de Rexel Une acquisition majeure augmentant significativement la présence de Rexel aux Etats-Unis, avec l’intégration d’une plateforme spécialisée dans les infrastructures ajoutant environ 1,1Md USD de chiffre d’affaires Une exposition accrue à des segments structurellement porteurs et à forte croissance, soutenue par une expertise reconnue et une offre de services à forte valeur ajoutée Une Valeur d’Entreprise de 1,4Md USD, reflétant un multiple de transaction attractif après synergies inférieur à Une opération répondant à l’ensemble des critères financiers de Rexel : un effet relutif sur les bénéfices par action dès la première année et une création de valeur en année trois, notamment grâce à un niveau élevé de synergies vers les objectifs financiers à moyen terme du Groupe Un financement équilibré préservant la flexibilité financière maintenir un ratio d’endettement proche de 2x à compter de 2027 Rexel a conclu un accord avec Audax Private Equity (« Audax ») en vue de l’acquisition de GCG, l’un des principaux distributeurs américains de câbles spécialisés, de solutions de connectivité, d’alimentation électrique et de solutions d’ingénierie destinées aux infrastructures critiques. Basé à Chicago (Illinois), GCG est présent sur 16 sites et emploie environ 950 collaborateurs. La société devrait atteindre un chiffre d’affaires de plus de 1,1 Md USD en 2026. Offre de services à forte valeur ajoutée, exposée à des segments en forte croissance GCG associe une expertise reconnue dans la distribution spécialisée à une offre complète de services à forte valeur ajoutée, comprenant notamment l’ingénierie, l’assemblage sur mesure, la modification de produits, le kitting, les tests et des capacités logistiques à forte réactivité. Une part significative de son chiffre d’affaires est générée par des offres propriétaires et plus de 75 % de ses revenus intègrent des produits ou services à valeur ajoutée. Ces savoir-faire permettent à GCG d’intervenir en amont dans la conception et la spécification des projets, d’aider ses clients à réduire les délais et coûts d’installation, et de développer des relations clients durables et fortement intégrées. Cette acquisition renforce l’exposition de Rexel à des marchés structurellement porteurs, soutenus par l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle, l’augmentation de la demande en électricité et les besoins croissants de modernisation des infrastructures. articles.title: REXEL:  Rexel to acquire GCG
articles.desc: Rexel to acquire GCG, a leading specialty infrastructure platform in the US, a key milestone on Rexel’s strategic roadmap
articles.content: a leading specialty infrastructure platform in the US, a key milestone on Rexel’s strategic roadmap Seizing a major opportunity to expand our US business, adding a c.$1.1bn sales specialty infrastructure platform $1.4bn Enterprise Value acquisition at an attractive x 2026e EBITDAaL multiple post run-rate synergies including EPS accretion in year 1 & value creation by year 3, supported by targeted Financed through a mix of existing cash on hand and debt, alongside an equity raise of up to €500m to preserve credit rating and balance-sheet flexibility. Remain committed to an indebtedness ratio of c.2x from 2027 onwards Rexel has entered into an agreement with Audax Private Equity (“Audax”) to acquire GCG, a leading US provider of specialty wire and cable, connectivity, power and engineered solutions for critical infrastructure applications. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, GCG operates 16 locations with approximately 950 employees and is expected to reach over $1.1 billion of revenue in 2026. Compelling value-added service, exposed to high growth segments GCG combines specialty distribution with a complete range of advanced services including engineering, custom assembly, product modification, kitting, testing and rapid fulfillment. A significant portion of its revenue is generated from proprietary offerings, while more than 75% incorporates value-added products or services. These capabilities allow GCG to participate further upstream in product design and specification, help customers reduce installation time and labor, and build more embedded customer relationships. The acquisition will position Rexel at the center of several powerful mega trends reshaping the global economy and its electrification. More than 60% of GCG's revenue is exposed to high growth segments including data centers, power/utilities infrastructure, grid modernization, communications, defense, utilities and other long-term growth markets where artificial intelligence, rising electricity demand and increasing technical complexity are driving sustained infrastructure investments. Since 2019, GCG has delivered double-digit annual revenue growth and is expected to reach a c.11% EBITA margin in 2026, reflecting GCG’s exposure to structurally attractive end-markets, proprietary products, technical expertise and its value-add operating model. Rexel’s Board of Directors has unanimously approved the acquisition of GCG. Executing our value creating M&A strategy This acquisition is fully aligned with Rexel’s strategy to accelerate further in its core geographies and is a strong driver of the Group’s accelerated sales growth. Rexel also expects to generate meaningful cost synergies from GCG through scale, logistics optimization, insourcing and select efficiencies. In addition, the combination also creates significant commercial opportunities by bringing GCG’s engineered solutions and specialty distribution capabilities to Rexel’s broader customer base. The transaction values GCG at an Enterprise Value of approximately $1.4 billion, corresponding to a <8x 2026e EBITDAaL multiple including anticipated run-rate synergies. This transaction respects all financial M&A criteria, including EPS accretion in year 1 and value creation by year 3. Rexel plans to finance GCG through a mix of existing cash on hand, and debt for c.€800 million. The Group also intends to raise up to €500 million equity through an accelerated bookbuilding offering (subject to market conditions), to preserve its credit rating and maintain a net financial debt / EBITDAaL ratio around 2x from 2027 onwards. As such, Rexel will maintain a balanced capital allocation strategy between a consistent dividend policy of at least 40% payout and a self-funded value creative acquisition strategy allowing the Group to continue delivering solid growth and returns to shareholders. The transaction is expected to close by 2026 year-end, subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions. Guillaume Texier,

articles.title: Epiq Acquires Canopy To Unite Cyber Incident Response Technology and Service Expertise
articles.desc: Canopy Brings Proven Breach Response Technology, AI Capabilities, and Cyber Expertise to Epiq Canopy Brings Proven Breach Response Technology, AI Capabilities, and Cyber Expertise to Epiq
articles.content: Epiq Acquires Canopy To Unite Cyber Incident Response Epiq Acquires Canopy To Unite Cyber Incident Response Technology and Service Expertise Canopy Brings Proven Breach Response Technology, AI Capabilities, and Cyber Expertise to Epiq NEW YORK, Sept. 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Epiq today announced the acquisition of Canopy, a leading data breach response technology company. The acquisition enables organizations to manage cyber incidents more efficiently and accurately by combining the Canopy platform with the global scale, cyber expertise, and ongoing AI investment of Epiq. “Canopy has been a longstanding partner to Epiq in helping organizations respond to cyber incidents,” said , Senior Vice President, Managed Services and Cyber Solutions at Epiq. “By welcoming its technology and engineering talent into our team, clients benefit from a more connected breach response experience. They gain next-generation cyber solutions that further reduce risk exposure through proactive preparedness and strengthen post-event response with AI.” The patented Canopy platform assesses exposed data, detects sensitive information, and identifies impacted individuals. Its Auto Review feature uses agentic AI to automate first-level data mining review, allowing teams to move directly from culling to quality control. The platform will be integrated into Epiq AI , and will be accessible through the Epiq Service Cloud, a that provides clients with streamlined access to cyber solutions. Epiq welcomes the Canopy team, including former Chief Operating Officer , who joins as Vice President, Product Management, Cyber. Elliott brings experience leading software and services businesses across legal technology, cyber incident response, and data-driven operations. “Canopy was built to support organizations in understanding the scope and impact of a cyber incident and responding with greater speed and confidence,” said Elliott. “With Epiq, we gain global resources and scale to build on the foundation that made Canopy successful and bring that technology to more organizations.” Canopy engineers and cyber response specialists also join Epiq to contribute to the development of Epiq AI for Cyber, expanding the capabilities available to organizations responding to cyber incidents. Epiq is a trusted partner to more than 87% of breach counsel and over 70% of cyber insurers. The company supports more than 1800 cyber incidents annually, delivering up to 95% data reduction using AI and facilitating up to 2 million notifications per day. Epiq AI for Cyber extends that work, continuing to drive innovation across the technologies and services organizations depend on to assess and respond to cyber incidents. Epiq, a technology and services leader, takes on large-scale and complex tasks for corporations, law firms, and the courts by integrating people, process, technology, and data intelligence. Clients rely on Epiq to streamline legal, compliance, and settlement administration workflows to drive efficiency, minimize risk, and improve cost savings. With a presence in 17 countries, our values define who we are and how we partner with clients and communities. Learn how Epiq and its 4000 people worldwide create meaningful change at epiqglobal.com.
